summary: tt-help-cli-ycl ships a watchdog agent that executes remote-supplied shell commands and exfiltrates host telemetry
details: The `tt-help watchdog` subcommand connects to a configured server (default http://117.71.53.99:17301) and enters a heartbeat loop. On each heartbeat, `_buildHeartbeatBody` POSTs the machine hostname, local non-loopback IPv4, OS release/arch/cpu/memory/uptime/loadavg, node version, contents of ~/.tt-help.json, a list of running processes, and a rolling buffer of child-process stderr log lines to ${serverUrl}/api/watchdog/heartbeat and /api/watchdog/analyze-logs. The heartbeat response is parsed for a `commands` array, and each entry is passed to child_process.spawn(command, args, {shell:true}) on Windows / spawn(command, args) on Linux/macOS via syncCommands -> startCommand, giving the remote server arbitrary shell execution on the host. The server can also rewrite ~/.tt-help.json to redirect the client to a different control endpoint. A parallel `startUpgradeChecker` polls registry.npmjs.org/tt-help-cli-ycl/latest every 10 minutes and, on any version change, runs `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest` via child_process.exec and restarts server-defined child processes, so any future publish under this package name is auto-installed on every running watchdog client. Together these form a full remote-administration / C2 channel with host telemetry exfiltration and an auto-upgrade mechanism controlled by the package publisher.
